content: The corrigenda for the WHO consolidated guidelines on tuberculosis, specifically Module 2 on systematic screening for tuberculosis disease, include the following updates: 1. On page vi, lines 13–15, the original contributors listed for PICO question 10 (accuracy of screening approaches in children and adolescents) were Anna Mandalakas, Tara Ness, and Bryan Vonasek (Baylor College of Medicine, USA), and Karen Steingart (Cochrane Infectious Diseases Group, Liverpool School of Tropical Medicine). This has been updated to include an additional contributor, Yemisi Takwoingi (University of Birmingham, United Kingdom). 2. On page vii, lines 3–9, the list of observers at the GDG meetings has been revised. The original list included Sevim Ahmedov and Charlotte Colvin (United States Agency for International Development, USA), Draurio Barreira Cravo Neto (Unitaid, Switzerland), Olivia Bierman (Karolinska Institute, Sweden), Michael Campbell (Clinton Health Access Initiative, USA), Pierre-Marie David (Université de Montréal, Canada), Christopher Gilpin (International Organization for Migration, Switzerland), Brian Kaiser (Global Drug Facility, Switzerland), and Mohammed Yassin (Global Fund to Fight AIDS, Tuberculosis and Malaria, Switzerland). The revised list now includes Jacob Creswell (Stop TB Partnership, Switzerland) as an additional observer. 3. On page 5, lines 23–25, the definition of systematic screening for tuberculosis disease has been updated. The original definition described it as the systematic identification of people at risk for TB disease in a predetermined target group using tests, examinations, or other procedures that can be applied rapidly. The revised definition now specifies that this process involves assessing symptoms in addition to using tests, examinations, or other procedures that can be applied rapidly. 4. In Web Annex C, the GRADE Evidence to Decision Tables have been replaced with a newly formatted version. However, no changes were made to the content itself. These corrections have been incorporated into the electronic version of the document.
